column1: # Shared conformance vectors for the Dead-words line. Identical, byte for byte, in claude-code-playbook and codex-playbook.
# Format: <expectation><TAB><the line, to end of line>. @F1@ and @F2@ are replaced by each edition with two file names legal there; both files exist.
# ok N    = the line parses; N fixed-string searches are made (items x files). Exit 0 or 1, never 2.
# error   = the line is a Dead-words line that does not parse. Exit 2.
# ignore  = the line is not a Dead-words line at all: zero searches, exit 0.
# Fail closed: the bare marker anywhere but the start of a line is an error, so an entry can never be skipped silently. Prose names the marker inside a code span.
# A line inside a fenced code block is ignored too; that needs more than one line, so each edition tests it separately.

column2: **Dead words:** `a carriage return at the end is allowed` (in `@F1@`)
Prose that mentions `**Dead words:**` inside a code span is not an entry.
Prose that mentions **Dead words:** bare in the middle of a line is refused, never skipped.
- **Override — rule 9.1.** **Dead words:** `marker not at the start of the line` (in `@F1@`)
**Dead words** `no colon, so not the marker` (in `@F1@`)
